title: Seed and rib fingerless mitts
subtitle: Fingerless mitts with alternating columns of seed stitch and 1x1 rib on the back of the hand.
excerpt: Fingerless mitts in DK wool with a textured stitch pattern combining seed stitch and 1x1 rib columns on the back of the hand. Plain 1x1 rib on the palm. Afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Seed stitch and rib combined in a striped column arrangement. The fingerless mitt construction is standard; the stitch combination is an original arrangement.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts x 28 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles. The seed-and-rib pattern pulls slightly narrower.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A textured stitch made by alternating knit and purl stitches in a way that they sit directly above a different stitch on the previous row: k over p, p over k. When worked in the round, the sequence alternates both stitch type and round. The result is a bumpy, non-curling fabric.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Fingerless mitts in DK wool with a textured pattern combining
seed stitch
and 1x1 rib columns on the back of the hand. Plain 1x1 rib on the palm.
Afterthought thumb
. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

The back of the hand uses a 4-stitch column repeat: 2 stitches of seed stitch beside 2 stitches of 1x1 rib. The two textures sit side by side and create a subtle ridged effect without a cable needle. The palm is plain 1x1 rib. The construction uses
magic loop
on a long circular. Budget about 80 g (175 m / 190 yards) of DK wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 80 g (about 175 m / 190 yards) of DK-weight wool

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 3: 1 for beginning of round, 1 for the palm/back divide, 1 for thumb

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 25 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the thumb

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles. The seed and rib panel pulls in slightly compared to stocking stitch; this is normal and does not change the palm width.
Stitch pattern

attrs.heading: Back-of-hand panel (worked over 20 sts, 4-stitch repeat, 2-round repeat)

items.name: Round 2
items.qty: *p1, k1 (seed reverse), k1, p1 (rib same)*; repeat 5 times.

content.text: The seed stitch columns alternate k-p and p-k on successive rounds. The 1x1 rib columns remain k-p on every round. The palm works as plain 1x1 rib throughout.
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 40 (44, 48) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 22 (24, 26) rounds of 1x1 rib.
Hand body

Place a marker at the midpoint to divide back (first 20/22/24 stitches) from palm (last 20/22/24 stitches). Begin the back panel pattern on the back stitches and continue 1x1 rib on the palm stitches. Work the 2-round repeat for 10 (12, 12) rounds.
Thumb and hand above

On the next palm section: work the first 10 (11, 12) palm stitches with waste yarn, slip back, and work in rib to the back marker. Continue the pattern for 18 (20, 22) more rounds. Bind off in 1x1 rib.
Thumb
Remove waste yarn. Pick up 10 (11, 12) stitches above and 10 (11, 12) below. Work 12 (14, 14) rounds of 1x1 rib. Bind off in rib.
Common faults

Seed stitch looks like rib: the columns were not alternated correctly between rounds. On round 1, the seed stitches must be k, p; on round 2 they must swap to p, k. Check the round marker position every repeat.
Back panel looks twisted relative to the palm: the back and palm stitch counts are unequal. Recount at the divide marker and adjust the cast-on if needed.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side.
Care
Hand wash in cool water. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next
Replacing the seed stitch columns with a simple cable cross gives the same back-of-hand emphasis with more definition. The mock cable fingerless mitts use the same column structure at the same gauge.
